content: Monarda didyma, commonly known as bergamot, scarlet beebalm, scarlet monarda, Oswego tea, or crimson beebalm, is an aromatic herb belonging to the Lamiaceae family. It is native to eastern North America, specifically from Maine westward to Ohio and southward to northern Georgia. The plant's name is derived from its fragrance, which is reminiscent of the scent of the bergamot orange. The scientific name honors Nicolas Monardes, who first described American flora in 1569. This herb typically grows to a height of approximately 1.5 meters. Its stems are square in cross-section, and the leaves are arranged oppositely along these stems. The leaves measure between 6 to 15 cm in length and 3 to 8 cm in width, displaying a dark green color with reddish veins and coarsely toothed margins. The upper surface of the leaves is either smooth or sparsely covered with fine hairs, while the underside has spreading hairs. Monarda didyma produces striking, ragged, bright red tubular flowers that are 3 to 4 cm long. These flowers are grouped in showy clusters of about 30, accompanied by reddish bracts. The plant thrives in dense clusters along stream banks, thickets, and ditches, with its flowering period occurring from July to late August. Bergamot is widely cultivated as an ornamental plant both within and beyond its native range. It has become naturalized in regions further west in the United States and in parts of Europe and Asia. The plant grows best in full sunlight but can tolerate light shade. It thrives in moist, well-drained soils. Numerous cultivars have been developed, offering a variety of flower colors ranging from white and pink to deep red and purple. The name Oswego tea originates from the Oswego Native Americans, who taught European settlers to use the plant for tea, particularly after the Boston Tea Party in 1773. The flowers and leaves of Monarda didyma are also popular ingredients for making potpourri. It is important to note that the bergamot herb is not the source of bergamot oil, which is used to flavor Earl Grey tea. That oil is derived from the bergamot orange, a citrus fruit native to the Mediterranean region.
